Public Sodick manuals confirm most core G, M, and T words on LN1W, LN2W, and LNW controls. They also show several differences and gaps against `assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps` and `docs/decisions/617-sodick-wire-post.md`.

All findings below come only from public Sodick documents and university lab guides. None come from CAM posts, CAM outputs, or proprietary sources.

Standard LN1W/LN2W sample programs use this word order: 4-digit `N` number, `G54`, `G90`, `G92` with `X` and `Y`, `G29`, `T94`, `T84`, `T80`, `T91`, `C` condition, cutting moves (`G01`, `G02`/`G03` with start-to-center `I` `J`), `G40` on a linear exit move, `T90`, optional `T81`/`T85`/`T87`, and `M02`. A second LN1W/LN2W form puts `C` condition parameter rows and `H` offset rows at the file head with `;` block ends before the `N` blocks.

## Findings Table

| Point | Finding | Source | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| LN1W, LN2W, and LNW core words (`G20`/`G21`, `G90`, `G54`–`G59`, `G00`, `G01`, `G02`/`G03` start-to-center `I` `J`, decimal point, `T91`/`T90`, `M00`/`M01`, `M02`, comments) | Confirmed. LN1W, LN2W, and LNW controls accept these Mark 21 G, M, and T words, decimal coordinates (such as `X10.5`), start-to-center `I` and `J` arcs, and `(...)` comments. | Sodick Inc., *Wire EDM Machine Operation Training — LN1W / LN2W Control* (P/N 6300015, Jan 2012), pp. 58–79 ([PDF](https://fab.cba.mit.edu/content/tools/sodick_edm/sodick_user_manual_small.pdf)); Sodick, *LPW / LQW / LQW DX / LNW Code Instructions* (Ver. 4.0), Ch. 1, 5, 9 ([PDF](https://machineryhost.com/sodick/LN/LPW-LQW-LNW-Code.pdf)) | stated in the source |
| Direct Sodick LN source (replaces 1998 summary fetch) | Confirmed for LN1W, LN2W, and LNW (including AQ600L). Official Sodick PDFs on public sites document these controls directly. | Sodick LN1W/LN2W Training Manual, pp. 1–119 ([PDF](https://fab.cba.mit.edu/content/tools/sodick_edm/sodick_user_manual_small.pdf)); Sodick LPW/LQW/LNW Code Instructions ([PDF](https://machineryhost.com/sodick/LN/LPW-LQW-LNW-Code.pdf)); Sodick *LNW HeartNC* & *LN UTY* Manuals ([LNW](https://machineryhost.com/sodick/LN/LNW.pdf), [UTY](https://machineryhost.com/sodick/LN/UTY.pdf)) | stated in the source |
| `M02` end word and no `M30` | Confirmed. Programs end with `M02`. The LN1W/LN2W manual states: "there is NO M30 end of program and rewind". | Sodick LN1W/LN2W Training Manual, pp. 58–59 ([PDF](https://fab.cba.mit.edu/content/tools/sodick_edm/sodick_user_manual_small.pdf)); Sodick LPW/LQW/LNW Code Instructions, Ch. 9 Sec. 1 ([PDF](https://machineryhost.com/sodick/LN/LPW-LQW-LNW-Code.pdf)) | stated in the source |
| Absence of `%` and `O` program number | Confirmed in examples. LN1W/LN2W sample programs omit `%` and `O`. The Code manual still lists `O` as an available program number address. | Sodick LN1W/LN2W Training Manual, pp. 68–79 ([PDF](https://fab.cba.mit.edu/content/tools/sodick_edm/sodick_user_manual_small.pdf)); Sodick LPW/LQW/LNW Code Instructions, Ch. 1 Sec. 3-1 ([PDF](https://machineryhost.com/sodick/LN/LPW-LQW-LNW-Code.pdf)) | seen in an example program |
| Wire-center path (no `G41`/`G42`) and `G40` during motion | Confirmed. A program without `G41`/`G42` cuts on the programmed wire path, and the control cancels offset with `G40` during movement. | Sodick LN1W/LN2W Training Manual, pp. 58–79 ([PDF](https://fab.cba.mit.edu/content/tools/sodick_edm/sodick_user_manual_small.pdf)); Sodick LPW/LQW/LNW Code Instructions, Ch. 5 ([PDF](https://machineryhost.com/sodick/LN/LPW-LQW-LNW-Code.pdf)) | stated in the source |
| `C` condition digit count (strictly 3 digits vs 1 to 4 digits) | Corrected. The post allows only `C` plus 3 digits, but LN docs show 1-digit `C1`, 3-digit `C000`, and 4-digit conditions (`0006`) in the "Cond. Num." field. | Sodick LN1W/LN2W Training Manual, pp. 68–79 & p. 115 ([PDF](https://fab.cba.mit.edu/content/tools/sodick_edm/sodick_user_manual_small.pdf)); MIT CBA Fab Lab, *Sodick SL400G Wire-EDM* ([page](https://fab.cba.mit.edu/content/tools/sodick_edm/)); Sodick LPW/LQW/LNW Code Instructions, Ch. 1 Sec. 3-10 "Machining Condition Number" ([PDF](https://machineryhost.com/sodick/LN/LPW-LQW-LNW-Code.pdf)) | seen in an example program |
| Bare `C` word vs condition and offset header rows | Corrected (both forms exist). LN1W/LN2W supports bare `C` calls into the control `Cond` memory table (pp. 68–79), or `C000` condition rows and `H000`/`H001` offset rows at the file head with `;` block ends (p. 115). | Sodick LN1W/LN2W Training Manual, pp. 68–79 & p. 115 / manual p. 104 ([PDF](https://fab.cba.mit.edu/content/tools/sodick_edm/sodick_user_manual_small.pdf)); MIT CBA Fab Lab, *Sodick SL400G Wire-EDM* ([page](https://fab.cba.mit.edu/content/tools/sodick_edm/)) | seen in an example program |
| Omitting tank (`T94`), flush (`T84`), and wire-drive (`T80`) T words | Corrected (warning gap). Neither `C` nor `T91` starts wire drive (`T80`), high flush (`T84`), or submerge (`T94`). Sample programs include all three; the post warns operators only about tank fill and flushing, not wire drive (`T80`). | Sodick LN1W/LN2W Training Manual, pp. 58–79 ([PDF](https://fab.cba.mit.edu/content/tools/sodick_edm/sodick_user_manual_small.pdf)) | stated in the source |
| `M02` safety after `T90` | Corrected (caveat). `T90` cuts the wire and `M02` ends program execution, but `T81` (wire drive off), `T85` (high flush off), and `T87` (pump off) are separate codes. Public docs do not confirm that `M02` stops wire feed or pumps by itself. | Sodick LN1W/LN2W Training Manual, pp. 58–79 ([PDF](https://fab.cba.mit.edu/content/tools/sodick_edm/sodick_user_manual_small.pdf)); Sodick LPW/LQW/LNW Code Instructions, Ch. 9 Sec. 1 ([PDF](https://machineryhost.com/sodick/LN/LPW-LQW-LNW-Code.pdf)) | stated in the source |
| LN Assist and SPW (Mark 25+) format rules | Not found. Corporate pages name LN Assist, SPW, and Heart NC, but no free official NC format manual for LN Assist or SPW exists on the open web. | Sodick Corporate Site ([site](https://www.sodick.com/)); Sodick *LNW HeartNC* Manual ([PDF](https://machineryhost.com/sodick/LN/LNW.pdf)) | not found |
| `G40` on a `G00` block (`G40 G00 X Y`) before `T91` | Not found. Manual examples place `G40` on linear retract or cutting moves (such as `G50 G40 Y0.`), not on a rapid `G00` block before `T91` when `G41`/`G42` never ran. | Sodick LN1W/LN2W Training Manual, pp. 58–79 ([PDF](https://fab.cba.mit.edu/content/tools/sodick_edm/sodick_user_manual_small.pdf)); Sodick LPW/LQW/LNW Code Instructions, Ch. 5 ([PDF](https://machineryhost.com/sodick/LN/LPW-LQW-LNW-Code.pdf)) | not found |
| Omitting `G92` and `G29` (`G54`–`G59` alone before `T91`) | Not found. `G54`–`G59` select resettable work systems `0`–`5`, but every LN1W/LN2W example writes `G92` and `G29` before `T91`. Public docs do not confirm if omitting `G29` breaks `T91` recovery or if an earlier `G92` shift stays active across `M02`. | Sodick LN1W/LN2W Training Manual, pp. 58–79 ([PDF](https://fab.cba.mit.edu/content/tools/sodick_edm/sodick_user_manual_small.pdf)) | not found |
| Omitting all `N` sequence numbers | Not found. All LN1W/LN2W sample programs use 4-digit `N` numbers (`N0000`–`N1005`), and the Code manual lists `N` in block order (`N`, `G`, coordinates, `T`/`H`, `C`, `M`). Public docs do not confirm if a file with zero `N` words loads cleanly. | Sodick LN1W/LN2W Training Manual, pp. 68–79 ([PDF](https://fab.cba.mit.edu/content/tools/sodick_edm/sodick_user_manual_small.pdf)); Sodick LPW/LQW/LNW Code Instructions, Ch. 1 Sec. 3-1 ([PDF](https://machineryhost.com/sodick/LN/LPW-LQW-LNW-Code.pdf)) | not found |

## Not Found

- **LN Assist and SPW (Mark 25+) dialect rules:** Public Sodick product literature does not publish an NC programming manual for LN Assist or SPW.
- **`G40` on `G00` before `T91`:** No public Sodick LN manual confirms whether `G40 G00 X Y` with no active `G41`/`G42` executes cleanly or causes a control alarm.
- **Omitting `G92` and `G29`:** No public Sodick LN manual confirms whether `T91` and wire-break recovery (`G13`/`G15`) work safely without `G29`, or whether a previous `G92` shift persists inside `G54` after `M02`.
- **Omitting `N` sequence numbers:** All retrieved LN1W/LN2W sample programs include `N` numbers, so support for `N`-less files remains unconfirmed.
- **Idle safety at `M02` and panel-only `T80`/`T84`/`T94`:** No public Sodick LN manual confirms that `M02` stops wire feed and flushing pumps without `T81`/`T87` or panel settings, or that a cut runs safely when the file omits `T80`, `T84`, and `T94`.

## Suggested Changes for `sodick-wire.cps`

- Allow `C` condition IDs with 1 to 4 digits (for example `C1`, `C110`, or `C0006`) instead of rejecting everything outside 3 digits.
- Add a header warning for wire drive (`T80`) alongside tank fill (`T94`) and flushing (`T84`), and note that operators must set or stop wire feed (`T81`) and pumps (`T87`) at the control unless an option adds T-codes.
- Update comments to state that operators can use pre-loaded control `Cond` entries or in-file `C` header rows, and that `H` offset rows are unused because the post writes a wire-center path.
- Flag `G40 G00`, omitted `G92`/`G29`, and omitted `N` numbers for an on-machine test, and adjust them if the control rejects them or carries over a prior `G92` shift.
- Keep `NOT VERIFIED ON A CONTROL` in the header until a machine owner confirms a clean dry run and test cut.

## Control Check Required

You must still check the program on a real Sodick LN control (LN1W, LN2W, or LN Assist) with a dry run before you cut a part. Public manuals do not replace an on-machine test for `G40 G00`, omitted `G92` and `G29`, omitted `T80`/`T84`/`T94`, omitted `N` numbers, or `M02` stop behavior.

Source facts for the Sodick post (public ESPRIT EDGE 2026.4 help page "EDM Custom Settings / Sodick", updated 2026-11-19, sent by spikeypineapple; facts about the **control** only, in our words, nothing from that CAM's own posts or output; use of public CAM-vendor documentation for control facts approved by mkinney 2026-11-21):

1. **Conditions can be defined in the program.** A program opens with a condition block: a comment naming the fields, then `Cnnnn = <fields>;` lines (4-digit numbers in that example, e.g. `C0000`..`C0003` for the cut passes and `C0904`.. for finishing). That example has 18 fields: `ON OFF IP HRP MAO SV V SF C PIK CTRL WK WT WS WP PC SK BSA` (the owner's AQ600L `COND.DAT` has the first 15). This is where the low numbers (`C000`-`C099`) used for most passes come from; they are not in `COND.DAT`.
2. **Wire offset = H registers set in the program**, three forms: `H001 = H001 + <value>`, `H001 = H001 + H700`, `H001 = <value>`. Newer linear controls (example AQ327L, AQ537L) also accept `FLAG7 D<value>` to apply one clearance to all H registers without changing them.
3. **Program words:** `G92` set-origin (optional); `G29` stores the main reference point used by the auto wire threader to recover after a wire break (start of program / cut-off); `M00` stop when there is no auto threader (manual thread or cut); `G53 Z<value>` moves the upper guide in machine coordinates to a safe Z before positioning between work offsets (maximum is machine dependent); statements end with `;`.
4. **Taper:** `TP` and `TN` words.
5. **Other control features named:** `CUTVEL(f1,f2,...)` line (ALN machines, SPW control), anti-rust unit, barreling control (CSP) whose availability is read from the second digit of the `BSA` field.

Not covered by that page: the exact threading/cut M or T words for the LN controls, the program header/O-number, and the meaning or units of each condition field.

**Known-good reference program** from a Sodick owner (spikeypineapple, AQ600L LN control): a hand-written, annotated one-pass program for a 10 mm square, posted on #617 (`demoprog.txt`). Hand-written by the owner, not another CAM's output. What it shows that our `sodick-wire.cps` output does differently (to work through on this issue):

| Topic | Known-good program | Our post today |
|---|---|---|
| Conditions | defined in the program: header comment with 17 field names (`ON OFF IP HRP MAO SV V SF C PIK CTRL WK WT WS WP PC SK`), then `C000 = ...` (approach and cut start) and `C001 = ...` | names a table number (`C110`, `C001`) with no definition |
| Wire offset | `H000 = +000000.010000`, `H001 = +000000.162000` in the program, `FLAG7 D0.0000`, cut with `G42 ... G40` | wire-centre path, `G40` only |
| Heights | `TP100.` and `TN0.0` before `G90` | not written |
| Start | `G90`, `T94`, `G29` (auto-threader reference point), `T84` (high-pressure flush), `G54`, `G00 X0. Y0.`, `Z0`, zero-taper move with `U0.`, `T91` (thread) | `G21 G90`, `G54`, `T91` |
| Cut | `G42 G01` into the profile; the overlap on its own line; `G40` lead-out | `G01` wire-centre moves |
| End | `M03` (auto-thread jump point), `T90` (cut wire), `G349 G449 G549 G649 G749 G149 G249`, `T87` (pump off), `M35` (drain tank), `M02` | `T90`, `M02` |
| Number format | every number has a decimal point or is `0.0` (`X5.`, `TP100.`) | already decimal |
| Comments | no escape characters, `#` or `[ ]` | (check) |
| Extra lines | `QAIC(...)` and `SFCC...` (owner: not needed for a first version) | none |

Open questions sent to the owner on #617: where the two conditions come from (not found in `COND.DAT`), how `C001` gets selected, which H `G42` uses, `TP`/`TN` meaning, what `T94` does.

Test parts used (SolidCraft `.sc` with drawing, STEP, PDF drawing, picture): https://github.com/mkinney/cam-tools-and-fixtures/tree/main/samples/edm-validation - EDM-T1 square, EDM-T2 2-axis block, EDM-T3 taper block.
